_comment: Sourcing per part. gen_bom.py marries this with the board. LCSC stock is from the date below and must be re-checked before ordering; marketplace links rot within months, the search terms do not.

120R term.note: Same series as the verified 10k. The C number could not be confirmed by search, look up the manufacturer part number on LCSC.

100nF.note: 1206 is a large package for 100 nF, hence 2.3 cents rather than a fraction of that. Nothing cheaper exists here: YAGEO CC1206KRX7R9BB104 (C82601) costs 0.037 EUR. Over a million in stock.

22uF 3V3 bulk.note: Half the price of the 25 V part (C12891, 0.24 EUR) for the same job. 6.3 V on a 3.3 V rail is roughly a factor of two margin, normal for X5R. Worth knowing: ceramics lose capacitance under DC bias, a 6.3 V part at 3.3 V keeps about half, so 11 to 13 uF rather than 22. Ample for holding up the rail when three transceivers key at once. For the full 22 uF take C12891 (25 V, keeps about 85 %) and pay 12 cents more.

TVS bidir.desc: TVS bidirectional SMF12CA, SOD-123FL, 12 V standoff, 200 W
links: SMF 200W SOD-123 TVS kit, 20 values x 10 pcs, bidirectional
TVS bidir.note: The land is universal: copper runs from 0.30 to 2.90 mm off centre, so SOD-123, SOD-123F, SOD-123FL, DO-214AC (SMA) and a plain 1206 all sit on it. SMF12CA in SOD-123FL is the cheap default. SMAJ12CA in SMA is the same diode at 400 W instead of 200 W, same 12 V standoff and the same breakdown window, and its feet reach 2.80 mm so it now lands properly rather than hanging off the end. VRWM 12 V, so it does not conduct at the +12 V common mode RS-485 allows, VBR 14.7 V, clamps at 19.9 V with 10 A. Two per port, A and B to GND. A varistor is no substitute, it would not clamp until about 40 V.

1000uF 35V.desc: Electrolytic 1000uF 35V radial, D13 x L20, 5 mm pitch

MF-R 30V.desc: Polyfuse Bourns MF-R500, 30 V, 5 A hold / 10 A trip, 10.2 mm pitch
MF-R 30V.note: The largest that fits the current placement: body 17.4 x 3.0 mm, 3.8 mm clear of the 1000uF can. Sits in the left and right hole (10.2 mm pitch). The MF-R900 (9 A, C208493) is the largest of the series but its body is 24.2 mm and would come within 0.40 mm of the can; both parts stand 20 to 25 mm tall. MF-RHT and MF-RG are 16 V parts above 1 A and unusable on 24 V.

74AHCT541 pixel buffer.note: AHCT or HCT, both have TTL input thresholds (VIH 2.0 V) and therefore switch reliably from the 3.3 V of the ESP32. The only difference is propagation delay, roughly 6 against 14 ns, irrelevant at 1250 ns per WS281x bit. LCSC does not stock the AHCT part in DIP, hence the marketplace sources. Which other types work and which do not is below.

rows: First choice. TTL thresholds (VIH 2.0 V), fastest of the usable ones.
Ample. A WS281x bit lasts 1250 ns.
ACT also has TTL thresholds. Stronger outputs, more supply noise.
HC has CMOS thresholds: VIH = 0.7 x VCC = 3.5 V at a 5 V supply. The 3.3 V from the ESP32 will not switch it reliably. The name differs by one letter.
AC also has CMOS thresholds. Same problem as HC.
Same pinout, but the outputs are inverted. The strip then sees the opposite of the data. Only usable if the firmware inverts.
Same package, but inputs and outputs are interleaved instead of side against side. Not a drop-in.
1.65 to 3.6 V only. Cannot output 5 V, which is the whole point here.
The thresholds are right, but the inputs sink 0.4 mA, quiescent current is many times higher, and the part is obsolete. It works, but there is no reason.
SO-20, TSSOP, SOIC. All surface mount, will not fit the DIP-20 land.

12-24V IN 24A.desc: Screw terminal, 2 pole, 5.08 mm pitch, 24 A

DC jack.desc: DC barrel jack, Kycon KLDX-0202 land, 3.5 A
DC jack.note: The land is Kycon specific, pin 3 offset by 4.7 mm. Generic DC-005 jacks do not fit.

links: 390R exists only in 0805 (C17655) and fits the 1206 land by hand if needed
330R bias+.note: Fail-safe bias on a 3.3 V bus needs more than 200 mV idle differential. With two terminators (60 R, the normal case once this board is the controller at one end) 330 R gives 275 mV, 470 R only 198 mV. Anything from 270 R to 430 R works, see the table. Bus loading 4.6 mA, which no RS-485 driver cares about, and 5 % tolerance is irrelevant for a bias resistor. The land takes anything from 0402 to 1206: copper runs 0.30 to 2.30 mm off centre, so every end cap lands on it, an 0402's at 0.25 to 0.50 as much as a 1206's at 1.10 to 1.60. The 390R that only exists in 0805 therefore goes in without any trickery.

22uF W5500.note: Local bulk right under the W5500 module, 2.5 mm from its 3V3 pin. The rail reaches that module through 62 mm of 0.60 mm track from the dev board's regulator, which is about 62 nH: a 50 mA step in 10 ns pulls 0.31 V out of the pin, and the 22 uF that was supposed to catch it sits 54 mm away at the other end of the board. DC was never the problem, that path drops 6.6 mV at 132 mA. Optional, like everything else here, but fit it if you use Ethernet.

1uF.note: The middle rung of the W5500's decoupling. Same Samsung series and package as the 100nF, so one reel family covers both. It closes a factor-220 gap: the rail had 100nF and 22uF and nothing between them.

330R pixel.note: Series damping in each pixel data line, right at the buffer. The 74AHCT541 switches in 3-5 ns into whatever length of unterminated wire you hang on the terminal, and that edge rings, overshoots into the first LED's input and radiates on the way. 330R overdamps it deliberately: at 800 kHz a bit is 300 ns, so a slower edge costs nothing, and it also limits the current if someone shorts the data pin to 5 V or GND. Same part as the RS-485 fail-safe bias, so no extra line on the order.

ESP32-S3 N16R8.note: The socket is laid out for 25.40 mm row spacing, one full pitch wider than the official Espressif DevKitC-1 at 22.86 mm. Board size 57.5 x 27.9 mm. Hold the seller's photo against a 1:1 printout of the footprint before buying.

MAX3485 DMXn.desc: MAX3485 TTL to RS-485 module, 3.3 V, with enable pin
MAX3485 DMXn.note: It must have the EN pin, otherwise no RDM. Pinout is GND/A/B on the left and EN/VCC/RXD/TXD/GND on the right. Note that RXD is the module's input and belongs on the ESP32's TX.

search.ebay: USR-ES1 W5500 SPI to LAN Ethernet

USR-ES1 W5500.note: Two rows of 6 pins, 20.32 mm apart. Listings describing '8 pins in a single row' are a different module. The RJ45 overhangs the board by 2.5 mm.

12-24V -> 5V buck.desc: DC-DC step-down to 5 V, adjustable, 1 A or more

search.amazon: MP1584EN DC-DC step down module 3A adjustable

12-24V -> 5V buck.note: MP1584EN rather than LM2596: the LM2596 module is about 43 x 21 mm and no longer fits the 40 x 22 mm envelope. The MP1584EN input is rated to 28 V, so a 24 V supply must not rise above that at no load. Set it to 5.0 V BEFORE soldering it in.

OLED SDA/SCL/VCC/GND.note: These ship in two pin orders that differ by VCC and GND. Read the module's own silk, not the product page.

EC11.desc: Rotary encoder EC11, 20 mm D-shaft, with push switch

search.amazon: EC11 rotary encoder 20mm shaft push switch
search.ebay: EC11 rotary encoder switch 20mm D shaft
search.aliexpress: EC11 encoder 20mm handle with switch 5 pin

EC11.note: The part inside every KY-040 module, without the little board and its three 10k pullups: ENC_A is GPIO42, ENC_B GPIO41 and ENC_SW GPIO21, all with internal pullups, so the resistors buy nothing. 12.4 mm can, 2.5 mm pin pitch, two mounting posts. Sold in tens for small money; any EC11 clone fits, the case and pin positions are the same across the family. Add a knob for a 6 mm D-shaft.

Tact 6x6 H30.desc: Tact switch 6 x 6 mm, through hole, 30 mm plunger

search.amazon: tact switch 6x6x30mm through hole long plunger

Tact 6x6 H30.note: The plunger length is the only thing that varies on this land - 5, 7, 9, 13, 17, 25 and 30 mm all use the same 6 x 6 footprint. 30 mm because the encoder shaft already stands 20 mm off the board, so anything shorter disappears behind the same front panel. Goes straight to GND, IO3 and IO46 pull up internally.

Blade fuse holder, alternative to the po.desc: Blade fuse holder, ATO/ATC mini, PCB mount, 10.2 mm pitch

search.amazon: mini blade fuse holder PCB mount ATO ATC
search.ebay: PCB mount mini blade fuse holder 10.2mm
search.aliexpress: ATO mini blade fuse holder PCB through hole

Blade fuse holder, alternative to the po.note: Alternative to the polyfuse, not fitted alongside it. Same two nets, its own two holes. A blade fuse blows once and is replaced; the polyfuse resets itself but runs warm and drops voltage while it holds.

ignore.PinHeader: 2.54 mm headers are not listed: one 40-pin strip to snap apart covers all the header positions. The Display row is the exception, see below.
ignore.header-1x03-P2.54-terminal: The three DMX rows: a 3-pin piece off the same header strip, or a 2.54 mm screw terminal if you would rather screw the XLR tails down. Both fit the 1.20 mm holes.
ignore.Display socket: The display sits on a 1x04 FEMALE socket, not a piece of header strip. PinSocket 1x04 P2.54, 8.50 mm tall, which lifts the OLED 10.9 mm off the carrier so it clears the modules around it. A male header there would put the glass almost flat on the board.

_price_basis: Prices in EUR per piece at SMALL quantity (the LCSC tier at MOQ), not the volume price. Converted at about 0.92 EUR/USD. Where a page could not be checked the value is an estimate and the stock column says ?.
